dashboards.title: Amazon API Gateway
dashboards.description: Amazon API Gateway: rest, http and websocket apis and their health, from CloudWatch.

definition.content:
## Amazon API Gateway

REST, HTTP and WebSocket APIs: requests, latency (p95 and p99) and how much of it the backend takes, client and server errors, and the stage cache. Collected by the [AWS integration](/integrations/aws).

dashboards.title: Application Load Balancer
dashboards.description: Application Load Balancer: application load balancers and their health, from CloudWatch.

definition.content:
## Application Load Balancer

Application Load Balancers: the health of their targets, traffic and response time (p95 and p99), and HTTP responses by where they came from, the targets or the load balancer itself. Collected by the [AWS integration](/integrations/aws).

source.metrics: aws-cdk-lib@2.275.0 (Apache-2.0), lib/*/lib/*-canned-metrics.generated.*; the other namespaces from their CloudWatch metrics pages of the AWS documentation (doc); CloudFront, ECS, ECS Container Insights, RDS, RDS Proxy and WAF as Datadog publishes them (scripts/aws-datadog-metrics.json)

dashboards.title: Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling
dashboards.description: Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling: auto scaling groups and their health, from CloudWatch.

definition.content:
## Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling

Auto Scaling groups: how many instances each wants, has in service and is still launching or terminating, against its minimum and maximum size. Group metrics must be enabled on each group to reach CloudWatch. Collected by the [AWS integration](/integrations/aws).

dashboards.title: Amazon CloudFront
dashboards.description: Amazon CloudFront: distributions and their health, from CloudWatch.

definition.content:
## Amazon CloudFront

Distributions: requests and bytes served from the edge, error rates by status code, the cache hit rate and origin latency (additional metrics, enabled per distribution), and the functions running at the edge. Collected by the [AWS integration](/integrations/aws).

dashboards.title: Amazon DocumentDB
dashboards.description: Amazon DocumentDB: documentdb instances and their health, from CloudWatch.

definition.content:
## Amazon DocumentDB

DocumentDB instances: CPU, open connections, read and write throughput and how long each engine has been up (a reset uptime is a restart or failover). Collected by the [AWS integration](/integrations/aws).

source.metrics: aws-cdk-lib@2.275.0 (Apache-2.0), lib/*/lib/*-canned-metrics.generated.*; the other namespaces from their CloudWatch metrics pages of the AWS documentation (doc); CloudFront, ECS, ECS Container Insights, RDS, RDS Proxy and WAF as Datadog publishes them (scripts/aws-datadog-metrics.json)

dashboards.title: Amazon DynamoDB
dashboards.description: Amazon DynamoDB: tables and their health, from CloudWatch.

definition.content:
## Amazon DynamoDB

Tables: read and write capacity consumed against what is provisioned, throttling, request latency and errors per operation, and global table replication. Collected by the [AWS integration](/integrations/aws).

source.metrics: aws-cdk-lib@2.275.0 (Apache-2.0), lib/*/lib/*-canned-metrics.generated.*; the other namespaces from their CloudWatch metrics pages of the AWS documentation (doc); CloudFront, ECS, ECS Container Insights, RDS, RDS Proxy and WAF as Datadog publishes them (scripts/aws-datadog-metrics.json)

dashboards.title: Amazon EC2
dashboards.description: Amazon EC2: instances seen from the hypervisor and their health, from CloudWatch.

definition.content:
## Amazon EC2

Instances seen from the hypervisor: status checks, CPU and burst credits, network and the EBS volumes attached to them. Memory and disk usage inside the instance come from the Agent, not CloudWatch. Collected by the [AWS integration](/integrations/aws).

source.metrics: aws-cdk-lib@2.275.0 (Apache-2.0), lib/*/lib/*-canned-metrics.generated.*; the other namespaces from their CloudWatch metrics pages of the AWS documentation (doc); CloudFront, ECS, ECS Container Insights, RDS, RDS Proxy and WAF as Datadog publishes them (scripts/aws-datadog-metrics.json)

dashboards.title: Amazon ECS
dashboards.description: Amazon ECS: clusters and services and their health, from CloudWatch.

definition.content:
## Amazon ECS

Clusters and services: CPU and memory used against what is reserved, and the traffic of services using Service Connect. Tasks and containers in more detail come from Container Insights or the Agent. Collected by the [AWS integration](/integrations/aws).

source.metrics: aws-cdk-lib@2.275.0 (Apache-2.0), lib/*/lib/*-canned-metrics.generated.*; the other namespaces from their CloudWatch metrics pages of the AWS documentation (doc); CloudFront, ECS, ECS Container Insights, RDS, RDS Proxy and WAF as Datadog publishes them (scripts/aws-datadog-metrics.json)

dashboards.title: Amazon ECS Container Insights
dashboards.description: Amazon ECS Container Insights: container insights for ecs and their health, from CloudWatch.

definition.content:
## Amazon ECS Container Insights

Container Insights for ECS: running, desired and pending tasks per service, CPU and memory used against reserved (per service and per task definition family), network, storage and restarts. Collected by the [AWS integration](/integrations/aws).

dashboards.title: AWS Lambda
dashboards.description: AWS Lambda: functions and their health, from CloudWatch.

definition.content:
## AWS Lambda

Functions: invocations, how long they run (p95 and the longest run, to compare with their timeout), errors and throttles, and concurrency. Traces, cold starts and memory come from the Datadog Lambda extension. Collected by the [AWS integration](/integrations/aws).

dashboards.title: Amazon RDS
dashboards.description: Amazon RDS: database instances and aurora clusters and their health, from CloudWatch.

definition.content:
## Amazon RDS

Database instances and Aurora clusters: resources and load, connections, query latency (Aurora adds per-statement latency and throughput), storage and I/O. Database internals come from the Agent’s database checks. Collected by the [AWS integration](/integrations/aws).

dashboards.title: Amazon S3
dashboards.description: Amazon S3: buckets and their health, from CloudWatch.

definition.content:
## Amazon S3

Buckets: their size and objects (daily storage metrics, published once a day for the day before), and with request metrics enabled on a bucket its requests, errors, latency and transfer. Collected by the [AWS integration](/integrations/aws).

dashboards.title: Amazon SQS
dashboards.description: Amazon SQS: queues and their health, from CloudWatch.

definition.content:
## Amazon SQS

Queues: messages waiting, in flight and delayed, what producers send and consumers receive and delete, how old the oldest message is, and the dead-letter queues collecting what failed. Collected by the [AWS integration](/integrations/aws).

dashboards.title: AWS WAF
dashboards.description: AWS WAF: web acls and their health, from CloudWatch.

definition.content:
## AWS WAF

Web ACLs: requests allowed, blocked and counted (the ALL rule is each web ACL’s total), the rules and rule groups that matched, bot control’s CAPTCHAs and challenges, and DDoS attack requests. Collected by the [AWS integration](/integrations/aws).

dashboards.title: Azure CDN
dashboards.description: Azure CDN: front door standard / premium and cdn profiles and their health, from Azure Monitor.

definition.content:
## Azure CDN

Front Door Standard / Premium and CDN profiles: requests at the edge by status group and endpoint, cache hits, latency to clients and to origins, origin health, WebSockets and the Web Application Firewall. Collected by the [Azure integration](/integrations/azure).

dashboards.title: Azure Virtual Machine
dashboards.description: Azure Virtual Machine: virtual machines seen from the host and their health, from Azure Monitor.

definition.content:
## Azure Virtual Machine

Virtual machines seen from the host: Resource Health, CPU and burst credits, memory, the OS and data disks, and network flows. Processes and file systems inside the VM come from the Agent. Collected by the [Azure integration](/integrations/azure).

dashboards.title: Azure Functions
dashboards.description: Azure Functions: function apps and their health, from Azure Monitor.

definition.content:
## Azure Functions

Function apps: executions and execution units (the memory-time a Consumption or Flex plan bills), HTTP-triggered requests with their status codes and response time, and each instance’s memory, connections and threads. Collected by the [Azure integration](/integrations/azure).
Execution units are memory × time in MB-milliseconds; divided by the executions they are what an average run costs.

source.metrics: MicrosoftDocs/azure-monitor-docs@5ea4a79919c6ead6918e867858271ad70412ebad (CC BY 4.0), articles/azure-monitor/reference/supported-metrics

dashboards.title: Azure Key Vault
dashboards.description: Azure Key Vault: key vaults and their health, from Azure Monitor.

definition.content:
## Azure Key Vault

Key vaults: API hits by activity (secrets, keys, certificates, authentication), their results by status code, availability, latency and how close each vault is to its throttling limits (saturation). Collected by the [Azure integration](/integrations/azure).

definition.title: Vaults with the most failed calls

original.title: Vaults with the most failed calls

definition.content: Saturation is the share of the vault’s request limits in use; Key Vault throttles at 100%.

dashboards.title: Azure SQL Database
dashboards.description: Azure SQL Database: single databases and their health, from Azure Monitor.

definition.content:
## Azure SQL Database

Single databases: CPU, DTU or vCore use, workers and sessions, connections that succeed and fail, deadlocks, storage and log I/O. Collected by the [Azure integration](/integrations/azure).

source.metrics: MicrosoftDocs/azure-monitor-docs@5ea4a79919c6ead6918e867858271ad70412ebad (CC BY 4.0), articles/azure-monitor/reference/supported-metrics

dashboards.title: Azure SQL Elastic Pool
dashboards.description: Azure SQL Elastic Pool: elastic pools and their health, from Azure Monitor.

definition.content:
## Azure SQL Elastic Pool

Elastic pools: the eDTUs or vCores their databases share, against the pool’s limit, the storage they fill, and the sessions, workers, log writes and tempdb that throttle a pool before CPU does. Collected by the [Azure integration](/integrations/azure).

dashboards.title: Azure Storage
dashboards.description: Azure Storage: storage accounts and their health, from Azure Monitor.

definition.content:
## Azure Storage

Storage accounts: availability, transactions by API and response type, end-to-end latency against server latency (the difference is the client and the network), ingress and egress, and hourly capacity. Collected by the [Azure integration](/integrations/azure).

source.metrics: MicrosoftDocs/azure-monitor-docs@5ea4a79919c6ead6918e867858271ad70412ebad (CC BY 4.0), articles/azure-monitor/reference/supported-metrics

dashboards.title: Azure App Service
dashboards.description: Azure App Service: web apps and their health, from Azure Monitor.

definition.content:
## Azure App Service

Web apps: requests and HTTP status codes, response time, and each instance’s CPU time, memory and queue. Function apps share this resource type and have their own dashboard (Azure Functions). Collected by the [Azure integration](/integrations/azure).

AlloyDB for PostgreSQL clusters by instance: CPU and the memory left, connections against the limit, backends and transactions, the columnar cache, wait events, read pool replication lag and cluster storage. Collected by the [Google Cloud integration](/integrations/gcp).

## Google Artifact Registry

Artifact Registry repositories: requests from clients pulling and pushing images and packages, Artifact Registry API calls and their latency, repository sizes and reads from remote upstreams against their quota. Collected by the [Google Cloud integration](/integrations/gcp).

dashboards.title: Google Cloud SQL
dashboards.description: Google Cloud SQL: what Cloud Monitoring reports for it, laid out for the service.

definition.content:
## Google Cloud SQL

Cloud SQL instances of every engine in one place: availability, failover and replica lag, CPU, memory and disk, connections, then what each engine reports: MySQL’s queries and InnoDB, PostgreSQL’s backends, transactions and Query Insights, SQL Server’s batches and buffer pool. Groups of an engine you don’t run stay empty. Collected by the [Google Cloud integration](/integrations/gcp).

dashboards.description: Google Compute Engine: what Cloud Monitoring reports for it, laid out for the service.

## Google Compute Engine

VM instances seen from the hypervisor: CPU and the time vCPUs wait to run, persistent disk throughput and latency, VPC traffic and firewall drops, and managed instance groups. Memory and file systems inside the guest come from the Agent or the Ops Agent. Collected by the [Google Cloud integration](/integrations/gcp).

dashboards.title: Google Cloud Storage
dashboards.description: Google Cloud Storage: what Cloud Monitoring reports for it, laid out for the service.

definition.content:
## Google Cloud Storage

Cloud Storage buckets: what they store by storage class (sampled once a day, so over a week), requests by method and response code, bytes sent and received, and Autoclass transitions and dual-region replication. Collected by the [Google Cloud integration](/integrations/gcp).

source.metrics: cloud.google.com/monitoring/api Cloud Monitoring metrics list (CC BY 4.0), metrics_gcp_*, metrics_kubernetes and resources

dashboards.title: Google Cloud Pub/Sub
dashboards.description: Google Cloud Pub/Sub: what Cloud Monitoring reports for it, laid out for the service.

definition.content:
## Google Cloud Pub/Sub

Pub/Sub topics and subscriptions: publish requests and their latency, messages delivered by pull or push and acknowledged, the backlog of undelivered messages and the age of the oldest unacked one, expired deadlines and dead letters. Collected by the [Google Cloud integration](/integrations/gcp).

source.metrics: cloud.google.com/monitoring/api Cloud Monitoring metrics list (CC BY 4.0), metrics_gcp_*, metrics_kubernetes and resources

dashboards.title: Google Cloud Run
dashboards.description: Google Cloud Run: what Cloud Monitoring reports for it, laid out for the service.

definition.content:
## Google Cloud Run

Cloud Run services by revision: requests by response class and their latency percentiles, container instances and how many requests each takes, CPU and memory utilization across instances, billable time and Cloud SQL connections. Collected by the [Google Cloud integration](/integrations/gcp).
